CFML Language Reference: Functions

StructFind

Looks up a key in a structure and returns its value.

Category

Structure functions

Syntax

StructFind(structure, key)

Parameters

structure
The structure to search.
key
The key to look up (not case-sensitive).

Returns

The value stored under the key.

Usage

If the key does not exist, an Expression exception is thrown, so test with StructKeyExists first.

StructFind(s, k) gives the same result as the bracket notation s[k] or, for a fixed key, s.key. It is useful when the key name is in a variable.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Capitals = StructNew()>
<CFSET Capitals.France = "Paris">
<CFSET Capitals.Japan = "Tokyo">
<CFSET Capitals.Peru = "Lima">
<CFSET Country = "Japan">
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>The capital of #Country# is <B>#StructFind(Capitals, Country)#</B>.</P>
</CFOUTPUT>
<CFTRY>
  <CFSET Temp = StructFind(Capitals, "Atlantis")>
<CFCATCH TYPE="Expression">
  <CFOUTPUT><P>Atlantis: <I>#CFCATCH.Message#</I></P></CFOUTPUT>
</CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>

See also

StructKeyExists, StructInsert, StructUpdate
